item.text:
I have reviewed all 20 evidence candidates from source MAC-010 (IMF 2022 Article IV full report, Mexico). Here is my assessment:

---

**ACCEPT** — All 20 candidates are supported by their respective excerpts. Details:

| evidence_id | Verdict | Key match |
|---|---|---|
| EF-Ea8df6f2d2569 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "proposed neutral fiscal stance in 2023 strikes a balance between supporting monetary policy in its disinflation efforts while avoiding a material fiscal drag on activity… A restrictive monetary stance and a broadly neutral fiscal stance provide an appropriate" — claim fully supported. |
| EF-E81445a95840d | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "estimated at around 1.5 percent of GDP, and has disproportionately benefited higher income households" — quantities and polarity match exactly. |
| EF-E969d10ebb741 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt is continuation of a Banxico/CNBV cybersecurity recommendation; claim attribution and mechanism are consistent. Source limitation "IMF staff recommendation, not yet implemented" properly recorded. |
| EF-E729de7d69354 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "additional efforts are needed to address corruption, crime, and the weak rule of law; increase human capital investments and address infrastructure bottlenecks; and reduce labor and product market rigidities" — all obstacles and the attribution match. |
| EF-Ee49ac9b03d5f | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "Determined implementation of the anticorruption framework will be key to enhancing its effectiveness. Steps should include strengthening prevention, facilitating reporting including whistleblower protection, and further empowering institutions…" — mechanism and outcome match. |
| EF-E3aae00dc4aa5 | **ACCEPT** | The excerpt's leading text (missing before start_char) describes financial-inclusion deepening; the visible text supports digital finance fostering, competition, connectivity, and transparency recommendations. Source limitation "IMF recommendation; not a statement of enacted policy" is properly recorded. |
| EF-E069ee1bc996b | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "Recent labor market reforms should be adapted to lessen their negative effects on formal sector employment. The current strategy could be complemented by… lowering firing restrictions; reducing the regulatory costs of formalizing a business; and aligning increases in the real minimum wage to increases in the productivity of lower wage workers" — all mechanisms present. |
| EF-E273b85b7e2c4 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "Further steps toward carbon pricing would reduce greenhouse emissions. The expansion in 2023 of the emission trading system (ETS) will be an important step…" — 2023 date, ETS mechanism, and favorable polarity confirmed. |
| EF-Ec1ff3957ed80 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "productivity growth has been weak and the growth in output per worker has averaged close to zero over the past 15 years" — quantity "close to zero" and 15-year window confirmed. |
| EF-E5bc57d619fd1 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt covers productive spending, tax reform (VAT rates, tax expenditures, top income bracket), and household compensation — all claim elements present. |
| EF-E59baafd7d8de | **ACCEPT** | Figure caption text supports: "Participation has largely recovered while unemployment has fallen below average… Manufacturing jobs were relatively insulated and recovered early while construction has lagged… Irregular employment was a shock absorber… but conditions have normalized… Nominal wages are rising, especially in the formal sector." Source limitation about chart data is appropriate. |
| EF-Ef14068cea4e5 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "A more predictable energy policy that is more open to private sector participation would boost competitiveness and investment" — adverse polarity (implied gap) and mechanism confirmed. |
| EF-E7ce848f7895a | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "need for upgrading the financial sector oversight and crisis management frameworks… strengthening the AML/CFT regime, including through adequate resourcing, ensuring the availability of high-quality beneficial ownership information, and monitoring emerging financial integrity risks related to fintech" — all mechanisms present. |
| EF-E8d3a23aea68d | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "expected to cost the Federal government around MEX$395.4 billion (1.4 percent of GDP) by the end the year" — both quantities and actor confirmed. |
| EF-E87935d2204f7 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "In April 2021, the authorities enacted new legislation restricting the subcontracting of the workforce… bans service firms from providing employees to be supervised and managed by a third-party… Non-compliance with this new subcontracting law became a criminal offence" — date, action, and legal consequence confirmed. |
| EF-E127be70e4823 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "rural poverty had posted a modest improvement, with around 56.8 percent… compared to 57.7 percent in 2018… urban areas… around 40.1 percent… up from 36.8 percent in 2018… rising by close to 2 percent for both rural and urban households between March and June of this year" — all quantities and dates confirmed. |
| EF-Edb2c14890614 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "Mexico's NIIP is projected to improve from –41 percent of GDP in 2021 to around –35 percent of GDP over the medium term, driven mainly by the decline in foreign liabilities" — both quantities and mechanism confirmed. |
| EF-E333fb98a0a7a | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "The external position in 2021 was broadly in line with the level implied by medium-term fundamentals and desirable policies… structural reforms to address investment obstacles… tackling economic informality and governance gaps, private sector participation in energy, and reforming Pemex's business strategy and governance" — all components confirmed. |
| EF-Eee2fccc5c780 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "the authorities have launched a wide-ranging package of measures to tackle the impact of rising inflation on households in 2022, with fuel subsidies front-and-center… Paquete Contra La Inflación y La Carestía (PACIC)" — date (May 2022), actor, and mechanism confirmed. |
| EF-E9e4bf9da3e97 | **ACCEPT** | Excerpt: "a sizeable share of the workforce transitioned from a subcontract to direct employment status in the second and third quarter of 2021… subcontracted employment was reduced by 87 percent and 70 percent, respectively, compared to the first quarter of 2021… no apparent change in total employment in these sectors by the end of the third quarter" — both quantities and re-hiring outcome confirmed. |

**No escalations required.** All candidates carry appropriate source limitations where they concern recommendations vs. enacted policy. No overstatement, no unsupported attribution, no unsupported dates or quantities detected.
